newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Analysts raise H&M sales view on Q1 data.
newsitem.headline: Analysts raise H&M sales view on Q1 data.

text.p: Swedish fashion retailer Hennes & Mauritz (H&M) raised market hopes when it unveiled a 30 percent rise in sales in the first quarter of 1997 with analysts on Friday raising forecasts for the rest of the year.
"H&M showed a growth that was stronger than I had expected and I think a 30 percent rise is a very strong result," said Roddy Bridge, analyst at James Capel.
"I have adjusted my forecast for Hennes & Mauritz upwards after these figures.
"It could still be a bit worse in the second half of 1997, affected by the dollar, but it is undeniably positive."
H&M said on Thursday that sales at its stores across Europe had risen 30 percent in the first three months of the year compared to the same period a year ago.
It also said the trend in sales and earnings continued to be positive.
"I think the aim to improve profitability in logistics will raise the margins in the company," said Swedbank analyst Mats Liss.
"A growth in sale of 30 percent is strong and is in line with forecasts."
The rise in sales prompted a lot of analysts to lift their sales forecasts for 1997.
"I adjusted my figure for sales in 1997 upwards," said one analyst.
"I think the increase in the number of stores to be opened this year is positive. The new boutiques are to be opened in areas where margins are higher which is positive."
In the financial year 1996/97 H&M planned to open 50 new stores across Europe, adding to its current list of about 450 stores.
The company has already decided that it will open its first outlets in Finland this autumn and in spring 1998 it will open stores in France.
On Friday H&M shares ended six crowns higher at 1,054 crowns.
